solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What could make you cross — an act not challengeable

indicators.note: the letters of the two clue words that follow could be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Someone asks what deed would really annoy you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' tells you to rearrange CROSS and AN ACT; 'What' and 'you' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred and inviolable is beyond any challenge or criticism.

clue.text: Place in Home Counties accommodating Italian

indicators.note: the region abbreviation takes in the other piece, as a host houses a guest

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, where the Home Counties lie around London

explanation.surface: An Italian is lodging somewhere near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or spot where something stands.

clue.text: Cold air rising round a summer celebration — restaurant looked for

indicators.note: the cold-and-air pieces wrap around the celebration, sitting either side of it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word air is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a fete is an outdoor fair, typically held in summer

explanation.surface: A breeze blows over a village fair while someone hunts for somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' works because this is a down clue; 'round' puts the fair inside the cold-air pieces. 'looked for' only joins the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service eating place.

clue.text: Insect's beginning to descend with bird appearing

indicators.note: in a down clue the opening letter of the insect's name drops down to the bottom

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A bug starts falling as a bird turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the start of LOUSE moves to the end, giving OUSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel (or ouzel) is an old name for the blackbird and related thrushes.

clue.text: Performer caught hidden in a lot of hair

indicators.note: the cricket letter is tucked inside the hair word, concealed within it

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something is snagged and lost in a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female stage or screen performer.

clue.text: Church is given order to secure right holy cloth

indicators.note: the church, is and order pieces hold another letter fast within them

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A church receives an order to protect its rights.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour; 'to secure' places the right letter just after the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom is the white robe put on a child at baptism.

clue.text: Fish or beef?

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of ponds and lakes
beef as slang verb, to grumble or complain

explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a common freshwater fish; to carp is to complain, as to beef is.

clue.text: Rodents hiding beneath a priestly garment

indicators.note: in a down clue the rodents sit underneath the A, below it in the grid

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: Mice are lurking under something.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a white linen cloth worn on the neck and shoulders by a priest at Mass.

clue.text: Shopper set out — female with a good idea of what is in store

definitions.text: female with a good idea of what is in store

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper lays out goods while a woman knows what the shop has for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in store' pretends to be about shops; it means what the future holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetess is a woman who foretells future events.

clue.text: 8 is on rota — I keep records

parts.note: the solution to 8 down is a female seer; Anna is the prophetess in Luke's gospel who greets the infant Jesus
a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A woman is put on the duty schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer at 8 down; Anna is the Biblical example. 'is on' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist is a chronicler who writes yearly historical records.

clue.text: Superior blokes getting drunk, rolling over, going around very loudly

indicators.note: the reversed drunkard's word circles the musical sign, enclosing it
the drunkard's word is tipped over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Posh men get plastered and tumble about making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' turns the drunkard round to TOS, and 'going around' wraps it about the musical very-loud sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs is British slang for upper-class, well-dressed people.

clue.text: Film-maker with exceptional art excited nation

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters of art are put out of their usual order
excited means the letters of nation are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A director with remarkable artistry thrills a country.
explanation.walkthrough: ART rearranges to TAR and NATION to ANTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American director of Pulp Fiction.

clue.text: What could be earliest workshops

indicators.note: asks which word the letters of earliest could become when rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what something might have been at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ateliers are artists' or designers' studios.

clue.text: Ancient character delivering beer to pub

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
PH, public house, as on old maps

explanation.surface: An old regular brings beer to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivering' and 'to' just link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the ancient Hebrew and Phoenician alphabets.

clue.text: Able to read with letters newly presented and enlarged

indicators.note: the letters of able to read are presented anew, in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone literate shows off their freshly delivered post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with letters' only joins; the indicator is 'newly presented'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborated means expanded upon in greater detail.

clue.text: Altar is to be shifted — ropes provided

indicators.note: the letters of altar and is are to be moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Church furniture is being moved, with cords supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: Lariats are lassos, long ropes with a running noose.

clue.text: Piece of furniture with strange charm, excellent, right?

indicators.note: strange means the letters of charm are put into an odd order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 serves as letter I

explanation.surface: Someone praises an oddly charming piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARM rearranges to ARMCH; A1, first-class, gives AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a comfortable seat with side supports for the arms.

clue.text: Suit in post with batch

parts.note: mail is post, letters delivered
a lot is a batch, as at auction

explanation.surface: A suit arrives in the post along with other items.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a one-piece swimsuit or a dancer's tights.

clue.text: Naughty ogler keeping clear glasses

indicators.note: the rearranged ogler holds the other piece within it
naughty signals the letters of ogler misbehaving into a new order

parts.note: nett means clear, as of profit after deductions

explanation.surface: A lecherous starer keeps a transparent view.
explanation.walkthrough: OGLER rearranges to LORGE, which holds NETT: LORG-NETT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held to the eyes on a long handle.

clue.text: A famous Donald Duck finished off his career

definitions.text: A famous Donald Duck finished off his career

parts.words: A famous Donald Duck finished off his career
parts.note: not the cartoon Donald: a great Australian cricketer whose last Test innings ended with a score of nought, a duck

explanation.surface: A well-known cartoon character's career comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Donald Bradman, cricket's greatest batsman, was out for a duck (zero runs) in his final Test innings in 1948. He is also this setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Bradman was the Australian batsman who scored nought in his last Test innings.

clue.text: Like some physics that's unclear, just a little muddled

indicators.note: the letters of unclear are only slightly jumbled to give the new word

explanation.surface: Some physics is a bit confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters of UNCLEAR swap, hence 'just a little'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Sounds like Ray becomes fatigued and goes to bed

indicators.note: signals that the answer is said the same way as the following phrase

parts.note: a man called Ray tires

explanation.surface: Ray gets weary and turns in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night.

clue.text: Conservative is entertained by nasty folks who discriminate against certain people?

indicators.note: the conservative and is pieces are hosted inside the nasty folks

parts.note: rats are contemptible, treacherous people

explanation.surface: A Tory is welcomed among unpleasant bigots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts the Tory and 'is' inside the nasty folks; the question mark admits the definition stretches a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Racists treat people unfairly because of their ethnicity.

clue.text: Part of business excluding British farm

indicators.note: the British letter is left out of the business part

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a company

explanation.surface: A firm's division leaves out a British farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for raising cattle.

clue.text: The French hospital set up, dealing with one organ of the body?

definitions.text: dealing with one organ of the body?

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
san, short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: A French hospital is established to treat one bodily organ.
explanation.walkthrough: LA SAN reversed is NASAL; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose.

clue.text: Expert not right — Heather is laughing

indicators.note: the right letter is not there, removed from the expert word

parts.note: crack as an adjective means expert, first-rate
ling is the common heather

explanation.surface: A specialist gets things wrong and Heather laughs at it.
explanation.walkthrough: CRACK without R is CACK; 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cackling is laughing loudly and harshly.

clue.text: Woman in sparkly diamonds

indicators.note: the woman's name lies inside the words sparkly diamonds, across the join

explanation.surface: A woman is dressed in glittering jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a woman's name.

clue.text: Some lament this being the last word?

indicators.note: some means only part of the word lament is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps a sad lament is the final say on the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the word that closes a prayer or hymn.

clue.text: What pleases palate in fizzy wine that goes to head after short time

indicators.note: after says the wine and head pieces come behind the short time, so it goes first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Sparkling wine quickly goes to one's head, pleasing the taste buds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the top of the body, or wine going to your head, but is a headland; 'that goes to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastiness is the quality of food being delicious to the palate.

clue.text: Bit of dope finally cured a stomach

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of cured

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: Some drug at last soothed an upset belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a drug but means information, as in 'the inside dope'.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information; dope is slang for information.

clue.text: English boy heading west in valley

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the pieces read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: An English lad sets off westward through a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Marine creature with brown star in vessel

indicators.note: the colour and star pieces go inside the vessel

parts.note: a can is a container
rust is a reddish-brown colour
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A brown starfish sits in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: RUST and ACE go into CAN: C-RUSTACE-AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustaceans are shelled sea animals such as crabs and lobsters.
